messages.subject: caching database queries
parts:
Hey!  I'm new to Shiny and can't quite figure out how to cache expensive database queries on a per-user basis.  In my server.R, I've got something like this for plotting a graph:

output$metricPlot <- renderPlot({
      if(input$graph=="Users"){
        p<-ggplot(data=data(), aes(as.Date(lubridate), sum, colour=name))+geom_point(aes(colour=name))+geom_line(aes(colour=name))+scale_x_date("Date")+scale_y_continuous("Users")
        print(p)
    }
})

and I pull the data like this:

data<-reactive({

      if(input$graph=="Users){

        query<-"SOME NASTY SQL"                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                   
        if(!exists("usersData")){
            cat("Doesn't exist...\n")
            usersData<-dbGetQuery(db, query)
            usersData                                                                                                                                                                                                
        } else {
            cat("Exists...")
            usersData
        }
})

What I'd like is for the DB query to run the first time each user opens a page and selects a particular graph.  But then in subsequent interactions (either switching back to that graph or in selecting various subsets) it just uses the version already in memory.  But I can't quite get the scoping to work out so that it doesn't always run the DB query.  I know this would work:

shinyServer(function(input, output) {

  # connect to db and run all queries at the top outside of other functions...                                                                                                                                                                                                                                  

...
...

}

but I don't want to run all of the queries up front like this because it takes a really long time to run them all.

Is there some way to make this work?  Apologies if this is a dumb question, but I've read everything that I can find about scoping and can't quite figure it out.

Thanks!

Michelangelo

messages.author: ca443e6eaa0e78ed
messages.subject: Re: caching database queries
parts:
Are you talking about a query that is the same every time, except for a parameter or three? Or are there three very different queries that you run, with an if/else or whatever that decides which one should be active?

If the former then consider using a memoized function that is declared at the location that you pointed out in your email ("I know this would work:").

If the latter, then perhaps make each of your queries its own reactive, and have the "data" reactive use each of them when appropriate.

Hope that helps...?

Awesome!  Thanks Joe!  It was the latter case, so I made each query its own reactive, as you suggested, and then the data reactive calls each one in turn.  That has the proper caching effect I was after.  

Also, didn't know about the memoized function.  I'm going to file that one away for some other time :)

Michelangelo
